transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (VelaScale Partnerships), Jasper Liu (VelaScale Head Cloud Alliances), Priya Menon (VelaScale Solutions Architect)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood intro, VelaScale capabilities, potential integration models (marketplace listing, reseller, joint pilot). Security and compliance quick check. Ask to run pilot benchmarks on Dedicated vs Private.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this motion, with me is Carlos Rivera, our solutions engineer, hey carlos.
[00:18] Carlos: Hey all, thanks for time, looking forward to unpacking how we might partner, I'll be more focused on the technical side.
[00:30] Anika: Hi, thanks Maya, Jasper and Priya here with me. Quick note we have limited time today so wanted to cover integration models and security.
[00:42] Jasper: Yeah, we get a lot of requests from customers wanting a managed LLM inference option that we can resell or integrate in the marketplace.
[00:55] Maya: Great context. high level from Redwood, we offer hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private/vpc installs. For partners we typically do three models: marketplace listing + referral, reseller with dedicated capacity for your customers, or a joint private deployment for regulated customers.
[01:18] Priya: Can you expand on the private option? We have a few financial customers that will only use VPC or on-prem.
[01:28] Carlos: Sure, Private is basically customer-controlled networking with our control plane optionally deployed in your environment. You get KMS integration, audit logs, and fine-grained RBAC. We also support HSM integrations for keystore. Note, sometimes the terminology in notes gets munged — it's k v cache in the runtime for prefix caching, not "k v cash" as i've seen auto transcripts show.
[01:52] Jasper: Nice. For marketplace / reseller, what does provisioning look like? Do we onboard customers into Redwood or you white-label?
[02:06] Maya: We generally keep the Redwood brand, but we can support co-branded flows. For reseller you can reserve dedicated capacity under your account and resell — we have APIs for tenant provisioning, usage metering, and billing hooks.
[02:20] Anika: Any constraints on GPU types? We often sell A100 and newer Ampere variants, but some enterprise customers want H100 or L40X.
[02:33] Carlos: We run on a range of hardware. Our runtime picks kernels and quantization profiles based on model and hw. H100 gives best perf for large context, but A100 and L40X are common too. We recommend we run a quick benchmark for your common models — that's usually the fastest way to qualify.
[02:52] Priya: How does quantization affect rmse... i mean quality? We've seen hallucination increase some, curious about your guidance.
[03:03] Carlos: Good question. quantization trades off fp16/INT8 to reduce memory and increase throughput. We provide profiles that are model-specific; our Redwood Optimize toolkit recommends the quantization level per workload. For each pilot we run generation quality checks against your eval set.
[03:24] Jasper: On the commercial side, curious how revenue share would work — is it per-token, per-seat, or a flat margin?
[03:34] Maya: We do a few approaches: usage-based per-token pricing is default for hosted. For reseller/dedicated we can do contract-based committed monthly capacity and share economics (margin on committed spend). We'll introduce the GTM team if we get further.
[03:48] Anika: Security — SOC 2, SAML/SSO, audit logs — do you have certs?
[03:56] Maya: We're SOC 2 compliant, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management, and audit logs are available in Console + export. For sensitive customers we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and keep keys customer-managed.
[04:15] Priya: Do you have a list of compliance docs? We need to share with our security team.
[04:20] Maya: Yes, i'll send the security pack — SOC2 report, data flow diagrams, and a KMS/HSM integration note.
[04:29] Jasper: Great. Technical: if we do dedicated capacity, what's the typical lead time to spin up a pool?
[04:36] Carlos: Depends on capacity size. Small pools (1-2 racks) can be provisioned in days, larger reserved contracts take longer and we coordinate region/hardware. Autoscaling with burst capacity is supported. We'll provide an operations runbook.
[04:55] Anika: How do you handle routing and fallback? For example if a reserved pool is full.
[05:02] Carlos: Smart routing — requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region). If dedicated pool is saturated we can fallback to hosted variants or cheaper model variants automatically to maintain SLAs. We also support canary rollouts and A/B testing.
[05:24] Jasper: For the pilot, what telemetry do you expose? We need token-level cost, latency breakdowns for billing.
[05:33] Maya: Console provides token-level cost, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks. We can also provide a CSV export or API for billing ingestion into your systems.
[05:45] Priya: For provisioning customers via the marketplace, is there an onboarding API? We want to automate tenant creation and SSO mapping.
[05:54] Carlos: Yes, there's a tenant provisioning API and scim for user mapping. We also provide webhook events for lifecycle changes.
[06:08] Anika: Ok can we talk about sample workload? Most of our customers run multi-user chat apps with 2-5 rps per tenant and spikes during business hours. Latency at 95th percentile should be under 500ms ideally.
[06:25] Carlos: Understood. We'll capture a sample profile. For those throughput/latency targets we usually recommend dedicated pools plus prefix caching to reduce per-token latency. Continuous batching helps throughput but we tune for latency SLOs.
[06:47] Jasper: Any limitations around data residency? Some customers require EU-only data at rest and in transit.
[06:55] Maya: We have region controls and can deploy private control planes in the customer's VPC or support region-limited hosting. We'll note the residency requirements in the pilot scope.
[07:10] Priya: Do you support model catalog import? Customers sometimes bring their own open models.
[07:17] Carlos: Yes, we can onboard customer models — we support multiple model formats and can run quantization/compilation to optimize kernels. There's a model onboarding flow and security review for customer-provided models.
[07:34] Anika: How about integrations with third-party SIs — is the partner allowed to resell dedicated capacity under their contract?
[07:43] Maya: Yes that's the reseller model we described. We can also do referral with tracking links if you prefer lighter touch. For reseller there are provisioning and billing hooks we expose. We'll share the partner integration checklist.
[07:59] Jasper: Would you be open to a co-marketing announcement if we run a joint pilot and show strong results?
[08:06] Maya: Absolutely, we typically do case studies and joint webinars for successful pilots.
[08:12] Priya: Technical question — how do you handle KV cache invalidation for multi-tenant workloads? We had issues previously where prefix caching leaked context in poor implementations.
[08:25] Carlos: We isolate caches per tenant and also have eviction and TTL policies. We also keep strict access controls so no cross-tenant leakage should happen; we log cache access for audits.
[08:41] Anika: Can you share a sample benchmark report? A spreadsheet with latency/throughput across H100/A100 for a 2k context model would help.
[08:50] Carlos: Yes, i'll share a Dedicated benchmark spreadsheet — it will include perf numbers for several model sizes and quantization profiles.
[09:00] Jasper: About the pilot timeline — we prefer a 4-6 week pilot: week 1 onboarding and small perf tests, weeks 2-3 run benchmarks and quality evals, week 4 integration and go/no-go. Thoughts?
[09:14] Maya: Sounds good and realistic. We'll need eval sets from you for quality regression checks.
[09:21] Priya: We'll put together an eval set and expected qps per tenant.
[09:26] Maya: Perfect. Also re commercial — i'll send a high-level commercial template (reseller vs referral vs co-sell) so your legal can start an initial review.
[09:36] Anika: Great. Any blockers you see from your side?
[09:40] Carlos: Nothing immediate; the only potential complexity is HSM integration for some customers but we've done that with a few customers.
[09:48] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[09:52] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps. I'll send: security pack, partner one-pager, and the commercial template. Carlos will share the benchmark spreadsheet and propose dates for the SE deep-dive. You (VelaScale) will share an eval set and a sample customer profile.
[10:12] Jasper: Sounds good. Also we'd like a short integration checklist so our engineering org knows prerequisites for marketplace onboarding.
[10:20] Maya: We'll include that in the partner one-pager.
[10:24] Anika: Any other questions?
[10:27] Priya: None from me, thanks.
[10:30] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links.
[10:32] Carlos: Thanks everyone.
